title: No Useless Words
note: He defines this as not saying words that bring no righteousness, wealth or pleasure to you or anyone. Householders can’t wholly avoid lies, and harsh words and backbiting are already dealt with, so useless words come next.

couplets.plain: Whoever speaks useless words, to the disgust of many, is scorned by all.
couplets.pm: Someone who says useless words that many wise people hear with distaste is scorned by all. When the wise dislike someone, the rest scorn them too.

links.quote: speaks useless words, to the disgust of many, is scorned by all

couplets.plain: Saying useless things in front of many is worse than doing unkind things to your friends.
couplets.pm: Saying useless words in front of many wise people is worse than doing hateful things to your friends. Such words bring even more scorn than such deeds.

links.quote: worse than doing unkind things to your friends

couplets.plain: Talk that spins out useless things says one thing by itself: the speaker has no goodness.
couplets.pm: The talk of someone who spreads out useless matters at length itself says, “This person has no justice.” You can tell it from the talk, so the talk is said to say it.

links.reason: Spinning out useless talk is itself a notice that the speaker has no goodness.

couplets.plain: Useless, graceless words said among many are unjust, and they take you away from all that is good.
couplets.pm: If someone says words among many that bring no use and have no quality, the words are unjust towards those people and strip the speaker of good qualities. Quality in words means sweetness, truth and the like.

links.quote: they take you away from all that is good

couplets.plain: If people of good nature say useless things, their worth and the respect it brings will leave them.
couplets.pm: If people of sweet nature, like water, say useless words, their excellence leaves at once, and the respect it brings goes with it. “If” shows that such people don’t say such things.

links.quote: their worth and the respect it brings will leave them

couplets.plain: Don’t call a person who keeps repeating useless words a human being. Call them chaff among people.
couplets.pm: Don’t call someone who says useless words again and again a person. Call them chaff among people, since they have no grain of understanding inside.

links.reason: Someone who keeps repeating useless words is denied the name of person and called chaff.

couplets.plain: Let the noble say things without goodness if they will. It is good that they say nothing useless.
couplets.pm: If the noble say words without justice, that can be let pass. If they can avoid saying useless words, that is good. “If they say” implies that they don’t. Useless words are worse than unjust ones.

links.quote: It is good that they say nothing useless
links.reason: Words without goodness may sometimes be allowed, useless ones never.

couplets.plain: Those wise enough to seek out rare gains won’t say words without great use.
couplets.pm: Those whose understanding can look into benefits that are hard to know won’t say words that lack great use. Those benefits are liberation, going to the higher worlds and the like. “Great use” rules out even words of small use.

links.quote: won’t say words without great use
links.reason: A mind that seeks out rare gains leaves no room for words of little use.

couplets.plain: Those of spotless sight, free of confusion, won’t say empty words even by a slip.
couplets.pm: Those whose understanding is pure and free of delusion won’t say useless words even by forgetting. Pure understanding means true knowledge.

links.quote: won’t say empty words even by a slip

links.remove: காட்சி here means understanding. The Tamil has no eye, whole or otherwise.

couplets.plain: Of words, say the ones with use. Of words, don’t say the ones without.
couplets.pm: Among words, say those that have use. Among words, don’t say those that have none. This sets down what should be said and what shouldn’t.

links.quote: Of words, say the ones with use. Of words, don’t say the ones without
